title: Characterization of randomized polynomial time
statement: For any function $p:\mathbb N\to\mathbb Q$ and any language $L$ of bit strings, the following are equivalent. First, there are constants $K,e\in\mathbb N$ and a finite nondeterministic Turing machine that, on each input $x$, halts on every choice string of length $K(|x|^e+1)$ and outputs the membership indicator of $L$ with probability at least $p(|x|)$. Second, there are constants $a,k\in\mathbb N$ and a polynomial-time Boolean verifier such that, for every input $x$, its acceptance probability over uniformly random bit strings of length $a(|x|+1)^k$ is at least $p(|x|)$ when $x\in L$, and its rejection probability is at least $p(|x|)$ when $x\notin L$.
hypotheses_covered: $p$ is a function from natural numbers to rational numbers
$L$ is a language of bit strings
